title: NASA's Big Plan: Build a Moon Base by 2032
summary:
NASA has big plans for the Moon. On Saturday, November 7, it said it will spend up to $10 billion to build a lasting moon base for astronauts by 2032.

The biggest part is a new plan called CLPS 2, worth up to $10 billion over ten years. NASA picked eight companies to take part, including Blue Origin, SpaceX and Lockheed Martin. NASA also raised the limit of its first CLPS deal from $2.6 billion to $4.2 billion.

NASA leader Jared Isaacman said the old deal worked for one or two trips a year. Doing more needs room to move things around.

The plan also has a robot rover called PROMISE. It runs on nuclear power and will explore the Moon's south pole from late 2028, using a drill to look for water ice. NASA gave Blue Origin $94 million to carry it to the Moon.

NASA also gave about $1.3 billion in launch work to other companies. All of this is part of NASA's Phase One plan, which runs through 2029. Phase Two, from 2029 to 2032, will keep building the base.
why_it_matters: A moon base could one day let astronauts live and work on the Moon, and the rockets and robots built for it are the same kind of science you might study in class or see in a museum.
